note: Company-level compliance: campaign SOPs, approval workflow, suppressions and channel rules. Brands inherit their company's profile; brand-level claims, safety text and do/don'ts stay in the brand kit. Every item names its source: an SOP document, 'Recommended practice' (industry norm, to confirm with the client) or a public regulation.

Cablivi.status_note: Sanofi SOPs haven't been provided. Cablivi uses the Novartis Flow Planner SOPs as a template; replace them once Sanofi's are uploaded. The brand plan itself only says to follow the local approval process (slide 2).

Flow Planner — HCP Target List Campaign, Segmentation Page
Flow SOP rules (block text, suppressions, task owners)

approval_workflow.source: Recommended practice (no MLR SOP provided). The brand plan's own assets carry approval codes such as MAT-IT-2500107 and MAT-GLB-2405864 (slides 28-29), consistent with this flow.

steps.what: Campaign brief with objective, audience, key messages and claims to be used
Copy and design built only from approved claims, with references annotated
Scientific accuracy; every claim matches its reference; on-label only
Comparative claims, trademarks, privacy and consent wording
Fair balance, safety information (ISI) placement, label consistency
Final sign-off; a unique approval code (e.g. MAT-XX-#######) printed on the asset
Local review before use in each market (required by the brand plan, slide 2)
Assets expire (typically 12-24 months) or on any label change; withdraw or re-approve

campaign_sops.name: DTC enrollment campaign — segmentation page
campaign_sops.applies_when: The campaign is triggered by an enrollment form sign-up (HQE 1.4.1 = Yes)
inputs: HQE form — Generic section (campaign name, code, goal)
HQE form — OMS Enrollment section (sources, codes, Q&A pairs)

steps.title: Confirm the inputs are complete
steps.rule: Start only when both inputs are gathered at pre-planning.

steps.title: Extract the campaign goal's rules
steps.rule: Pull out the enrollment source, segment names and business rules before drawing anything.

steps.title: Build the kit code
steps.rule: Source and Fulfilment Campaign Code both carry the Generic campaign code; the kit legend below is constant.

steps.title: List every enrollment source
steps.rule: One entry per source with its campaign source code, including sources the flow doesn't use.

steps.title: Draw the entry
steps.rule: Campaign code, the selected enrollment source and dispositions 4 & 26 only.

steps.title: Deduplicate
steps.rule: Dedupe and pick the disposition by latest response timestamp to set cadence timing.

steps.title: Apply eligibility checks in order
steps.rule: Hidden consent Q&A pairs first, then MDS suppressions (valid email), then campaign-specific Q&A — wording verbatim.

steps.title: Handle transitions and source-specific paths
steps.rule: Unbranded→branded transitions merge into the branded segment; source-specific Q&A splits into parallel journeys.

steps.title: Place the segment
steps.rule: Segment name comes from the campaign goal; it's the last node on the page.

open_items: Segment name should be an explicit field, not free text (B1)
Draw all hidden consent pairs or a subset? (B2)

campaign_sops.name: HCP target-list campaign — segmentation page
campaign_sops.applies_when: The audience is an MDS target list, not enrollment sign-ups (HQE 1.4.1 = No)

steps.title: Title block
steps.rule: Campaign name and campaign source code.

steps.title: Kit legend and task owners
steps.rule: Six-state kit legend; a task-responsibility key whose colours mark the nodes each team owns.

steps.title: Reference panels
steps.rule: List the MDS suppressions and any extra business rules (HQE 1.7.13).

steps.title: Entry and suppression stack
steps.rule: Draw the full suppression stack in the fixed order — even suppressions that exclude nobody. It is a compliance record.

steps.title: Segments
steps.rule: Specialty-based segments from HQE 1.7.5, names taken as given.

steps.title: Version history
steps.rule: Version, date, change and author for every substantive change.

open_items: Is the task-owner team list fixed per campaign? (A1)
Confirm the canonical suppression order and that none may be omitted (A3)
Restricted-state list fixed or per campaign? (A5)
Mixed HCP/DTC campaigns — which SOP governs? (A7)

DTC.source: SOP-01 v0.5, step 7 and Annex A

rules.why: Consent to company communications (Novartis in the template)
Valid email; no-DM-address and invalid-DM exclusions

rules.code: IMDNA Kaiser list, per campaign code

channel_rules.rule: Send only with email consent; include unsubscribe; honour opt-outs within 10 business days; ISI or a link to it in every promotional email
channel_rules.source: CAN-SPAM Act; FDA OPDP fair-balance expectations

channel_rules.rule: Approved templates only; reps may not edit claims
Unbranded ads carry no product name or claim; branded ads need ISI or a one-click link; retargeting only with retargeting opt-in
channel_rules.source: FDA guidance on character-limited media; SOP-01 Q50610

channel_rules.rule: HCP-only content behind an HCP gate; patient site in plain language with full ISI
Speaker slides MLR-approved; off-label questions routed to Medical Information
No more than 1 promotional email per HCP per week per brand unless the campaign type allows (cadence set per campaign type)

prelaunch_checklist.item: Every asset has an MLR approval code and an expiry date
Every claim traces to an approved claim and reference
ISI / fair balance present or linked on every promotional asset
Local approval obtained for each market
Segmentation page built per SOP-01 (DTC) or SOP-02 (HCP)
Full suppression stack drawn in the reference order
Consent checks applied before any send or retargeting
Version history row added for this change
First-use submission to FDA (Form FDA 2253) planned for US promotional materials

regulatory_baseline.name: FDA prescription drug advertising (fair balance)
regulatory_baseline.what: Promotion must be truthful, balanced between benefit and risk, and consistent with the label

regulatory_baseline.name: Form FDA 2253 — first-use submission
regulatory_baseline.what: Promotional materials submitted to FDA (OPDP) at the time of first use

regulatory_baseline.name: PhRMA Code on Interactions with HCPs
regulatory_baseline.what: Rules on HCP interactions, speaker programmes, meals and educational items

regulatory_baseline.name: EFPIA Code of Practice
regulatory_baseline.what: Promotion to HCPs, interactions, disclosure of transfers of value

regulatory_baseline.name: No DTC advertising of prescription drugs
regulatory_baseline.what: Prescription medicines can't be advertised to the public; patient content must be disease-awareness only

regulatory_baseline.name: CAN-SPAM
regulatory_baseline.what: Commercial email: accurate sender, unsubscribe, opt-outs honoured within 10 business days

regulatory_baseline.name: GDPR & ePrivacy consent
regulatory_baseline.what: Consent or another lawful basis for processing; prior consent for marketing email

regulatory_baseline.name: HIPAA (patient data)
regulatory_baseline.what: Protected health information from covered entities needs authorisation for marketing use
